read: full: all 26 pages (abstract; sections 1-9; dataset access; references). Figs 1-5 are images with no text layer.
venue_now: Not shown in the text: the file is the arXiv 2603.02239 preprint with no journal header (p.1). The catalogue's 'Computers & Industrial Engineering 2026' (doi 10.1016/j.cie.2026.112333) is not confirmed by this file.
what_it_is: ERI is a taxonomy-driven instruction dataset for training and evaluating engineering LLMs: nine fields x 55 subdomains x seven intent types (definition, explanation, calculation, comparison, design, troubleshooting, code) x three difficulty tiers, 50 records per cell, 57,750 records (p.1, p.5). Both the instructions and the reference responses were generated by an LLM (GPT-5 Mini) from (field, subdomain, intent, difficulty) seed tuples, five pairs per API call and ten calls per seed (p.9, p.18). Seven models were evaluated on a stratified 10% subset (over 5,000 items each) and each response was scored 1 to 5 against the model-written reference by three LLM judges from different providers, averaged (p.13-14). In place of human checking, a 'convergent validation' from frontier-model scores bounds hallucinated references at 1.7% (p.1, p.18).
domain: engineering: civil, mechanical, electrical, chemical, environmental, aerospace, materials, industrial, fire science (9 fields, 55 subdomains; Table 1, p.6). Covers all five EngTrace branches.
size: 57,750 instruction-response records in 1,155 cells (p.1, p.5). The released splits listed on p.22 total 53,429 (train 45,415, validation 2,671, test 5,343). Seven models evaluated, each on a stratified 10% subset of over 5,000 items; 115,962 judgments (p.13-14).
source_of_items: generated by an LLM: GPT-5 Mini writes both the question and the reference answer from a taxonomy seed tuple (p.9, p.18). Filtering: schema validation, exact deduplication on the lowercased instruction, optional semantic deduplication, length filters; GPT-5.1 rates a random 10% on a five-point quality scale (p.12).
instances: static: generated once by an LLM and released as fixed JSONL splits (p.9-10, p.22); nothing is regenerated at evaluation time.
has_gold_traces: no: the reference responses are model-written free text. For calculation items the success criteria ask for 'key steps for auditability' (Table 2, p.7) and references 'typically contain a numeric result and units' (p.12), but no intermediate value is computed or verified, and the paper acknowledges 'the absence of human-verified ground truth' (p.18).
evaluation: LLM judge, holistic per response: three judges (Claude Haiku 4.5, GPT-4.1 Mini, Mistral Small 3) each give a 1-5 score against the reference answer and the mean is taken (p.14). The harness also has automatic checks for empty outputs, refusals and missing final answers, plus a constraint-satisfaction flag when a bound in the prompt can be parsed (p.12-13). No step-level scoring.
human_validation: None reported. The reported checks are inter-judge Spearman 0.70 to 0.80 with within-one-point agreement above 85% (p.14), a GPT-5.1 quality rating of a random 10% of records (p.12), and the convergent-validity analysis: frontier models score 4.0 or above on 68.8% of items, and only 1.7% of items have frontier scores at or below 3.0, which the paper calls an empirical bound on hallucinated references (p.18). Expert validation of a stratified subsample and a human-verified gold subset are future work (p.18, p.20).
contamination_measures: none: deduplication (p.12) targets redundancy, not contamination, and the train, validation and test splits are all public on Hugging Face (p.22).

engtrace_use.explanation: Candidate; the May paper does not cite it. ERI itself cites EngTrace (ref. [29], arXiv 2511.01650, accessed 31 January 2026; p.25) and quotes it as an 'entirely synthetic' dataset, in support of its own LLM-based generation (p.9).

suggested_wording: ERI (Naser et al., 2026) covers nine engineering fields with 57,750 instruction-response records, but both its questions and its reference answers are written by an LLM, and responses are scored on a five-point scale by a panel of LLM judges against those references, with no human-verified ground truth.
facts_to_cite: 57,750 records over nine engineering fields, 55 subdomains, seven intent types and three difficulty tiers (p.1, p.5)
Questions and reference answers generated by an LLM (GPT-5 Mini) from taxonomy seed tuples, 50 per cell (p.5, p.9, p.18)
Seven models evaluated on a stratified 10% subset (over 5,000 items each) (p.13, p.15)
Each response scored 1 to 5 against the reference answer by three LLM judges from three providers (Claude Haiku 4.5, GPT-4.1 Mini, Mistral Small 3), averaged; 115,962 judgments (p.14)
The paper names 'the absence of human-verified ground truth' as a concern and bounds hallucinated references at 1.7% through frontier-model agreement, not human checking (p.18)
Expert validation of a subsample is left to future work (p.18, p.20)
Frontier models score above 4.30 of 5 (GPT-5 4.48, Claude Sonnet 4 4.31, DeepSeek V3.1 4.30) (p.1, p.14)
overlap_with_engtrace: Shares: multi-branch engineering scope that includes all five EngTrace branches (civil, mechanical, electrical, chemical, industrial; Table 1, p.6); three difficulty tiers (p.7-8); synthetic construction at scale; awareness of judge circularity, met with a multi-provider judge panel (p.14, p.18). Lacks: gold answers computed rather than written by a model (references are GPT-5 Mini output, p.18); generated instances (static, with a public test split, p.22); gold intermediate steps or values; step-level evaluation (one holistic 1-5 score per response, p.14); expert validation of the evaluator (only judge-judge agreement, p.14); any contamination control. What EngTrace adds beyond it: answers and milestones computed by the template code and checked deterministically, a private-seed pool, and a residual judge validated against expert step labels.
notes: (1) ERI cites EngTrace's arXiv version by name and title as 'entirely synthetic' (p.9, ref. [29] p.25). The revised text should draw the distinction (LLM-written records against template-generated items whose answers are computed by code) without revealing authorship under ARR anonymity. (2) Its circularity defence says the generator, evaluated models and judges 'share no training pipeline' (p.18), yet OpenAI supplies the generator (GPT-5 Mini), the quality rater (GPT-5.1, p.12), one evaluated model (GPT-5) and one judge (GPT-4.1 Mini) (p.14); this is a fair contrast with EngTrace's roster rule but is an observation, not something the paper states. (3) Internal inconsistencies: the conclusion expands ERI as 'Engineering Reasoning and Intelligence' (p.21) against 'Instruction' in the title; 'Data is available on request from the author' (p.22) beside the public Hugging Face links; the released splits on p.22 sum to 53,429, not 57,750 (presumably after filtering, which the paper does not state). (4) Scores fall from undergraduate to professional to graduate, so the graduate tier, not the professional one, is hardest (p.17). (5) The web search note's description is accurate on the points checked.
